public_body: Chatham Affordable Housing Trust Board Of Trustees
overall: The AG found the AHT Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law: the notice's 'Project Status Updates' topic was specific enough, and the RFP vote arose from a Select Board meeting less than 48 hours earlier. Communications allegations were declined.

allegations.summary: Aug 7 notice's 'Project Status Updates' for two properties allegedly did not disclose the planned vote to ask the Select Board to let the AHT Board run an RFP.
allegations.key_passage: Both properties were identified by address, or at least by street name.

allegations.summary: The AHT vote to petition the Select Board for RFP oversight allegedly should have been postponed until it could be placed on a posted notice.
allegations.key_passage: As the Select Board meeting occurred less than 48 hours prior to the AHT Board meeting of August 7, a discussion and vote regarding AHT Board oversight of an RFP could not reasonably have been anticipated at the time of posting notice for that meeting.

allegations.summary: Board members allegedly made disparaging comments about the Select Board, which the complaint said should have been listed separately on the notice.
allegations.key_passage: did not require separate mention on the notice of the August 7 meeting.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged improper communications among AHT members while preparing the board's response to the Open Meeting Law complaint.
allegations.key_passage: those allegations will not be reviewed here, as they would more appropriately be raised in a new complaint.
